answers: They again did evil in the sight of the Lord
easy.explanation: Judges 4:1 says that Israel again did evil in the sight of the Lord.
easy.q: What did the children of Israel do after Ehud was dead?

answers: The hand of Jabin king of Canaan
easy.explanation: The Lord sold Israel into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan.
easy.q: Into whose hand did the Lord sell Israel?

easy.explanation: Deborah was a prophetess and judged Israel at that time.

answers: Because they did evil in the sight of the Lord
medium.explanation: Their oppression followed Israel’s evil actions before the Lord.
medium.q: Why were the children of Israel delivered to Jabin and Sisera?

medium.explanation: The children of Israel came up to Deborah for judgment.
medium.q: What role did Deborah perform for the children of Israel?

answers: Under the palm tree of Deborah, between Ramah and Bethel
medium.explanation: The verse places Deborah under her palm tree between Ramah and Bethel.
medium.q: Where did Deborah sit when Israel came to her?

answers: After Ehud died, Israel did evil and was delivered to an enemy
Ehud’s death caused Deborah to leave Israel
challenge.explanation: The passage links Ehud’s death with Israel again doing evil and being sold into Jabin’s hand.
challenge.q: What connection does the passage make between Ehud’s death and Israel’s oppression?

answers: Deborah had public authority to lead and judge
challenge.explanation: The people sought Deborah’s judgment, showing that she held recognized authority.
challenge.q: What can be learned from the fact that the children of Israel came to Deborah for judgment?

answers: She ruled the land as a foreign queen
She exercised authority in deciding matters among the people
challenge.explanation: The context shows Deborah serving as Israel’s judge and leader.
challenge.q: What does “she judged Israel” most nearly mean in this context?

paragraphs.title: Barak’s Mission and Preparation for Battle

easy.explanation: Deborah called Barak the son of Abinoam out of Kedeshnaphtali.
Barak was told to take ten thousand men from Naphtali and Zebulun.
easy.q: Which tribes was Barak commanded to gather?

easy.explanation: Barak said he would go if Deborah went with him.
easy.q: What did Barak ask Deborah to do?

medium.explanation: The Lord said He would draw Sisera to the river Kishon.
medium.q: To what place was Sisera to be drawn?

answers: The journey would not be for Barak’s honour
medium.explanation: Deborah agreed to go, but said the journey would not be for Barak’s honour because the Lord would sell Sisera to a woman.
medium.q: What would result from Barak’s request that Deborah go with him?

answers: Lead his forces toward Mount Tabor
medium.explanation: The command directed Barak to go toward Mount Tabor with the Israelite forces.
medium.q: In the command “Go and draw toward mount Tabor,” what was Barak told to do?

answers: Because Barak would not go to battle
Because the Lord would sell Sisera into the hand of a woman
challenge.explanation: Deborah announced that Sisera would be delivered into the hand of a woman.
challenge.q: Why did Deborah say that the victory would not be for Barak’s honour?

answers: Deborah commanded the mission, and Barak agreed only if she went with him
Deborah commanded Barak to surrender, and he refused
Deborah commanded Barak to remain in Kedesh
challenge.explanation: Barak accepted the mission but conditioned his going on Deborah’s accompanying him.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between Deborah’s command and Barak’s response?

answers: She had no connection with the mission
She accompanied the army and exercised prophetic authority
challenge.explanation: Deborah went with Barak and announced what the Lord would do in the battle.
challenge.q: What does Deborah’s decision to go with Barak show about her role?

paragraphs.title: The Armies Assemble and the Battle

easy.explanation: Heber the Kenite had separated from the Kenites and pitched his tent near Kedesh.
Sisera gathered nine hundred chariots of iron.
easy.q: How many iron chariots did Sisera gather?

answers: He got down from his chariot and fled on foot
easy.explanation: Sisera lighted down from his chariot and fled away on his feet.
easy.q: What did Sisera do after the Lord discomfited his army?

answers: Because he heard that Barak had gone up to Mount Tabor
Because Deborah called him for judgment
Because Heber asked him for help
medium.explanation: Sisera was told that Barak had gone up to Mount Tabor, so he gathered his forces.
medium.q: Why did Sisera gather his chariots and army?

answers: She urged Barak to rise and go forth
medium.explanation: Deborah told Barak, “Up; for this is the day.”
medium.q: What did Deborah do when the time for battle came?

answers: The Lord threw him and his army into confusion and defeat
medium.explanation: The Lord discomfited Sisera, his chariots, and all his host before Barak.
medium.q: What does “the Lord discomfited Sisera” mean?

answers: The chariot was given to Barak
He got down from it and fled on foot
challenge.explanation: After the Lord defeated the army, Sisera left his chariot and fled on foot.
challenge.q: Why did Sisera no longer continue using his chariot?

answers: All Sisera’s host fell by the sword, and no man was left
challenge.explanation: The passage says that all Sisera’s host fell and there was not a man left.
challenge.q: What was the result of Barak’s pursuit?

answers: The Lord merely watched the battle
The Lord delivered Israel to Sisera
The Lord discomfited Sisera and his host before Barak

challenge.q: How is the Lord’s part in the battle described?

easy.explanation: Sisera fled to the tent of Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite.
Jael opened a bottle of milk and gave him drink.
easy.q: What did Jael give Sisera to drink?

answers: A tent nail and a hammer
easy.explanation: Jael took a nail of the tent and a hammer and fastened the nail into the ground.
easy.q: What did Jael use to kill Sisera?

answers: There was peace between Jabin’s house and Heber’s house
medium.explanation: The passage explains that there was peace between Jabin and the house of Heber.
medium.q: Why did Sisera think he could find safety with Jael?

answers: She returned him to his chariot
She invited him in, covered him, and gave him milk
medium.explanation: Jael told him not to fear, brought him into the tent, covered him, and gave him milk.

answers: A container used for holding a drink
medium.explanation: Jael opened a bottle, or container, of milk and gave it to Sisera.
medium.q: What is a “bottle of milk” in this passage?

answers: Jabin’s wife sent him to Barak
challenge.explanation: Jael, a woman, killed Sisera as Deborah had foretold.
challenge.q: How was Deborah’s announcement about Sisera being delivered to a woman fulfilled?

answers: She showed him the dead Sisera
She sent him to search Mount Tabor
challenge.explanation: Jael showed Barak the man he sought, and Sisera was dead with the nail in his temples.
challenge.q: What did Jael do after Barak came to her tent?

answers: She killed him, covered him, and gave him drink
She gave him drink, covered him, and killed him
She covered him, killed him, and called the army

challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes Jael’s actions?

easy.explanation: God subdued Jabin king of Canaan before the children of Israel.

Jabin was subdued before the battle
medium.explanation: After Sisera’s army was defeated and Sisera died, God subdued Jabin.
medium.q: What was the connection between Sisera’s defeat and Jabin’s subduing?

answers: Israel’s strength increased and overcame Jabin
medium.explanation: The phrase describes Israel growing stronger against Jabin until his rule was destroyed.
medium.q: What does “the hand of the children of Israel prospered, and prevailed” mean?

medium.explanation: To subdue Jabin was to bring him and his rule under defeat and submission.
medium.q: What does “God subdued” mean in this passage?

answers: Israel changed from being oppressed to becoming strong enough to break Jabin’s rule
Israel changed from freedom to oppression
Israel changed from victory to flight
challenge.explanation: Israel began under Jabin’s oppression but became strong and destroyed his rule.
challenge.q: What change in Israel’s condition is shown throughout the chapter?

challenge.explanation: The verse directly says, “So God subdued…Jabin.”
challenge.q: Who is identified as the source of Jabin’s subduing?

challenge.explanation: Israel prevailed against Jabin until they had destroyed Jabin king of Canaan.
challenge.q: What final result is described in these verses?
